reason: The text emphasizes hierarchy through multiple structural elements: (1) Joshua and the princes (נְשִׂיאֵי) exercise binding authority over the assembly—their oath sworn in God's name is upheld despite public complaint (וַיִּלֹּ֥נוּ כָל־ הָעֵדָ֖ה עַל־ הַנְּשִׂיאִֽים); (2) Joshua questions and judges the Gibeonites directly, exercising command authority; (3) The Gibeonites are assigned to explicitly subordinate, servile roles as חֹטְבֵ֥י עֵצִ֛ים וְשֹׁ֥אֲבֵי מַ֖יִם (woodcutters and water carriers), establishing clear status differentiation; (4) The narrative validates the princes' hierarchical authority—when the people complain, the leadership structure persists unchanged, implicitly endorsing hierarchy as legitimate and binding, especially when ratified by oath before God.
